seoTitle: Truck Accident Lawyer in Royal Oak, MI: I-696 and I-75, Woodward, Downtown Deliveries, the Federal Trucking Rules, and the Evidence That Expires
seoDescription: Hit by a semi, box truck, or delivery truck in Royal Oak? 2,081 heavy trucks and buses were involved in Oakland County crashes in 2024. Learn how the federal trucking rules, the carrier’s $750,000-plus insurance, underride guards, and Michigan no-fault apply to a crash on I-696, I-75, Woodward, or a downtown street, which agency owns the road, and why the logs must be preserved within days. sections.heading: Where Royal Oak truck crashes happen

c.v: I-696 and the I-75 interchange.
The freeway crashes are:
Backups:

items.v: rear-end and underride crashes in the stop-and-go at the I-75 interchange and the Woodward exit.

c.v: Lane changes:

items.v: trucks moving into a car in the blind spot on the right side of the cab, where the exits and entrances come close together.

c.v: Merges:

items.v: crashes on the ramps.

c.v: Work zones:

items.v: crashes during the long-running rebuilds of the I-75 and I-696 corridors.

c.v: A car that strikes the side or rear of a trailer can go under it. That is an
underride

crash, among the deadliest in trucking. Trailers must carry rear impact guards that meet federal standards (49 CFR 393.86). A missing, damaged, or substandard guard is evidence against the carrier and the trailer’s owner. In a work zone, the contractor can share responsibility.
Woodward and the Michigan lefts.

A tractor-trailer or long box truck making a U-turn at a Woodward turnaround may be too long to clear the median crossover in one move. When that happens, it blocks the lanes. Other truck crashes on Woodward:

items.v: trucks unable to stop for a changing signal at the mile roads
wide right turns onto Eleven, Twelve, Thirteen, and Fourteen Mile that catch a car on the inside of the turn

c.v: On designated Michigan routes, heavy trucks can weigh up to 164,000 pounds, about twice the federal Interstate limit. They need far more distance to stop.
Downtown deliveries.
Downtown’s restaurants, bars, and stores are supplied by box trucks and beverage trucks. Those trucks:

items.v: double-park in travel lanes
stop in bike lanes and crosswalks
back into alleys and loading zones
make tight right turns at Main, Washington, Fourth, and Eleven Mile

c.v: The crashes involve cars, cyclists, and pedestrians. Many happen in the morning delivery hours, and some at night. Where a business’s delivery arrangements routinely put trucks in the street, the business can share responsibility with the carrier. See our
pedestrian accident page
and our
bicycle accident page
The hospital campus.
Corewell Health’s Thirteen Mile campus receives a steady stream of supply, linen, food-service, and medical-gas trucks. Those trucks turn into and out of the campus.
Construction trucks.
New apartment and mixed-use buildings downtown and along Woodward bring dump trucks, cement mixers, and equipment haulers onto narrow streets. Their crashes involve:

items.v: trucks pulling out of sites
trucks backing without a spotter
spilled loads

c.v: Garbage trucks and delivery vans in the neighborhoods.
Garbage and recycling trucks, package vans, and furniture trucks work Royal Oak’s grid of residential streets. The crashes are:

items.v: backing crashes
crashes with vehicles stopped in the lane
children and pedestrians struck by a truck pulling away from the curb

c.v: Delivery vans are often operated by contracted delivery companies rather than by the retailer named on the package. The van’s operator, its insurer, and the contract between them have to be identified.
Lost and spilled loads.

Cargo, equipment, construction debris, or gravel that falls from a truck is a violation of the federal cargo securement rules (49 CFR 393.100 and following) and of Michigan law (MCL 257.720). The carrier and the company that loaded the truck can both be responsible.
Whose road it is.
Royal Oak is a city, and the road owner can be any of three agencies:

items.v: MDOT for I-696, I-75, and Woodward. A road-defect claim against the State goes to the Court of Claims, with written notice filed there within 120 days (MCL 691.1404).
The Road Commission for Oakland County for Ten, Twelve, and Fourteen Mile. Written notice is due within 120 days (MCL 691.1402, 691.1404).
The City of Royal Oak for the other streets, including Eleven and Thirteen Mile, downtown, and the residential streets. Written notice is due within 120 days.

c.v: The split follows the City’s road overview.

sections.heading: Who is responsible, and who pays

c.v: The carrier, not just the driver.

The motor carrier is responsible for its drivers’ compliance with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations. It is liable for a driver’s negligence in the course of employment. Michigan applies the federal rules to intrastate carriers (MCL 480.11a). A local hauler, a delivery carrier, or a construction trucker that never leaves Oakland County is held to the same standards as an interstate carrier.
These are the rules that decide truck cases most often:

head.v: What it means for the case

CDL, medical certificate, driving record, background check. Negligent hiring and retention are claims against the carrier.
Alcohol within 8 hours and drugs within 32 hours after a fatal crash, or after an injury or tow-away crash with a citation.
Pre-trip inspections, defect reports, maintenance records. Brake, tire, lift-axle, lighting, and reflective-tape cases are maintenance cases.
Loads must be contained or secured so they cannot shift or fall. A spilled load is evidence of a violation.
Equipment: rear impact guards, lighting, reflectors
Underride guards (393.86) and conspicuity marking. A trailer that cannot be seen at night or lacks a working guard is a defective trailer.
No handheld phone use. Reduce speed or stop in snow, ice, and fog.

c.v: The owner of the truck or trailer.

In Michigan, a vehicle’s owner is liable for its negligent operation by someone driving with the owner’s consent (MCL 257.401). When the tractor, the trailer, and the driver belong to different companies, each may be a defendant, although a company in the business of renting or leasing vehicles is generally shielded from owner liability by federal law (49 USC 30106).
Michigan no-fault still applies to you.
Your own auto insurer pays these benefits regardless of fault (MCL 500.3107):

items.v: your medical bills
85 percent of lost wages, up to the monthly cap DIFS sets each year
replacement services
attendant care

c.v: Written notice is due within one year (MCL 500.3145(1)).

Your claim against the driver and the carrier is for pain and suffering and for losses beyond no-fault. It requires a threshold injury (MCL 500.3135) and must be filed within three years (MCL 600.5805(2)). Michigan’s comparative fault rule is modified, not pure:
More than 50 percent at fault:

items.v: you cannot recover pain-and-suffering damages.

c.v: 50 percent or less:

items.v: your share reduces them (MCL 500.3135(2)(b); MCL 600.2959).

c.v: The noneconomic damages caps apply to medical malpractice and to product liability claims, such as a claim against the maker of a failed part (MCL 600.1483, 600.2946a), not to the claim against the driver and carrier.

The difference from a car case is the money available: the carrier’s $750,000-plus policy, often with excess coverage above it. If the carrier’s coverage still falls short, your own underinsured motorist coverage may add to it. Your insurer’s written consent is needed before you accept the carrier’s limit. See our

c.v: If you were the truck driver.

Workers’ compensation pays your benefits, and your employer usually cannot be sued (MCL 418.131). If you were injured in your employer’s truck, no-fault benefits generally come from the insurer of that truck (MCL 500.3114(3)). They are coordinated with comp, which is paid first (MCL 500.3109(1)). You can also sue a third party, such as another driver or a business whose dock or yard caused the crash. See our

faqs.question: How many truck accidents happen in Royal Oak?

answer.v: The State does not publish truck crash figures by city. Countywide, 2,081 heavy trucks and buses were involved in Oakland County crashes in 2024. Statewide, 15,888 crashes involved a heavy truck or bus, and 110 people were killed.

faqs.question: A delivery truck was double-parked downtown and I hit it, or swerved and hit something else. Whose fault is that?

answer.v: It depends on the facts. A truck stopped in a travel lane without warning, or in a place where stopping is prohibited, can carry fault. So can the business whose deliveries routinely put it there. Your own speed and attention matter too.

faqs.question: A box truck turned right and hit me on my bike. Who is responsible?

answer.v: Usually the truck driver, who must yield to a cyclist traveling straight. A truck’s right-side blind spot is no excuse for turning across a cyclist. The carrier and, if the driver was making a delivery, sometimes the business are part of the claim.

faqs.question: A semi was making a U-turn at a Woodward turnaround and blocked the road. Whose fault is the crash?

answer.v: It depends. A truck driver who makes a turnaround the truck cannot safely clear, or who blocks lanes without warning, can be at fault. So can a driver who was following too closely or speeding.

faqs.question: My car went under the back of a trailer on I-696. Is that the truck’s fault?

answer.v: It may be partly or wholly. Trailers must carry rear impact guards built to federal standards. A guard that is missing, bent, or too high to stop a car is evidence against the carrier and the trailer’s owner. The trailer has to be inspected before it is repaired.

faqs.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover from a trucking company?

answer.v: Not on pain and suffering against the driver or carrier. Michigan’s damages caps apply to medical malpractice and product liability claims. In practice, the limit is the insurance available: the carrier’s policy, any excess policy, and your own underinsured coverage.

faqs.question: Why does the lawyer need to act within days?

answer.v: Because the records expire. Hours-of-service logs must be kept for six months and inspection reports for three. Camera footage lasts days or weeks. The truck’s electronic data and the trailer’s damage can disappear when the truck is repaired.
